questions.prompt: Two departments occupy different IP subnets on separate VLANs. Their switch forwards frames only at Layer 2. Which additional capability is required for the departments to exchange IP packets?

choices.text: A larger dynamic MAC table
choices.explanation: More MAC entries do not provide inter-subnet forwarding.

choices.text: IP routing between the VLANs
choices.explanation: A router or routing-enabled Layer 3 switch connects their IP networks.

choices.text: A shared SSID
choices.explanation: An SSID identifies a wireless network, not an inter-VLAN route.

choices.text: PoE on both uplinks
choices.explanation: Electrical power delivery does not route IP packets.

questions.explanation: Each VLAN provides a separate Layer 2 domain. Communication between its IP subnet and another subnet requires a Layer 3 forwarding function.

questions.prompt: A switch uplink must cross an electrically noisy production area. Cable length is within both candidate Ethernet standards, and power delivery is unnecessary. Which property favors optical fiber over copper?

choices.text: Fiber does not carry data as electrical current susceptible to electromagnetic pickup
choices.explanation: Its optical signaling avoids electromagnetic induction into the data signal.

choices.text: Fiber always supports any optic regardless of wavelength
choices.explanation: Optic wavelength and fiber compatibility still matter.

choices.text: Fiber eliminates the need for link-budget checks
choices.explanation: Optical loss and receiver limits still constrain a link.

choices.text: Fiber supplies DC power to remote endpoints
choices.explanation: Optical fiber does not itself deliver PoE.

questions.explanation: Fiber is useful where electromagnetic interference or electrical isolation is a concern. It still requires compatible optics, cabling, and acceptable optical loss.

questions.prompt: A replacement copper cable restores a full-duplex Ethernet link. Over the next hour, CRC errors stop increasing while old error totals remain visible. Which conclusion is justified?

choices.text: The replacement failed because cumulative errors remain nonzero
choices.explanation: Historical counters do not have to reset when a fault is repaired.

choices.text: The subnet mask repaired the frame checksum
choices.explanation: IP addressing does not repair physical frame corruption.

choices.text: The observed error rate fell to zero during the measurement interval
choices.explanation: The unchanged cumulative counter means no additional counted CRC errors appeared.

choices.text: Every application transaction must now succeed
choices.explanation: A clean link does not prove higher-layer service success.

questions.explanation: Compare counter deltas over a known interval. The evidence supports improved link integrity during that interval, not a guarantee about every application.

questions.prompt: A sensor application sends independent UDP measurements. Packet 71 is lost, but packet 72 arrives. No application retransmission or ordering mechanism exists. What can the receiver expect from UDP itself?

choices.text: UDP requests packet 71 before exposing packet 72
choices.explanation: UDP has no such sequence-based recovery service.

choices.text: Packet 72 may be delivered without recovering packet 71
choices.explanation: Independent datagrams do not wait for missing earlier datagrams.

choices.text: UDP resets the connection after the missing packet
choices.explanation: UDP does not maintain a TCP-style connection to reset.

choices.text: UDP reconstructs packet 71 from its checksum
choices.explanation: A checksum detects some corruption; it cannot reconstruct lost payload.

questions.explanation: UDP can deliver a later datagram even when an earlier one was lost. If the application needs recovery or sequencing, it must use additional mechanisms.

questions.prompt: A dynamic MAC entry maps host H to Gi1/0/2 in VLAN 30. H is moved to Gi1/0/8 and immediately sends a valid frame there. Both ports are forwarding access ports in VLAN 30 and no security restrictions apply. What happens to H’s entry?

choices.text: It remains on Gi1/0/2 until the complete aging interval expires
choices.explanation: New source traffic can update a dynamic entry before aging.

choices.text: It is permanently installed on both ports
choices.explanation: Ordinary dynamic learning updates the source location.

choices.text: It changes to Gi1/0/8
choices.explanation: The newly observed source location replaces the old dynamic mapping.

choices.text: The destination MAC is assigned to Gi1/0/8 instead

choices.explanation: The priority portion is compared before the MAC portion of the sender bridge ID.

choices.text: SW-B, because its MAC address is lower.
choices.explanation: Its larger priority makes its complete bridge ID worse despite the lower MAC.
